name: Urban Climate Commons
summary: Studies how shade, building materials, and neighborhood design change street-level heat. The team connects temperature sensors with public-health surveys to understand unequal exposure during hot summers.
focus: How can cities protect people from extreme heat without displacing residents?

name: Coastal Water Studio
summary: Builds small sensors for tracking salt and pollutants as rivers meet the ocean. Computer models connect rainfall and tides to drinking-water quality in coastal settlements.
focus: Predicting where floodwater will contaminate freshwater supplies.

name: Accessible Robotics Workshop
summary: Designs affordable assistive robots that help people with limited mobility reach objects and navigate homes. Human-centered experiments combine computer vision, safe motion planning, and adjustable physical interfaces.
focus: Robotic assistance that adapts to a person's daily routines and physical abilities.

name: Trustworthy Models Group
summary: Examines when machine-learning predictions fail for groups underrepresented in training data. Researchers build transparent evaluation tools for classifiers used in public services and study privacy-preserving learning.
focus: Making prediction errors and dataset limitations understandable to affected communities.

name: Neural Recovery Lab
summary: Investigates how nervous systems recover movement after injury. Wearable electrical sensors and interactive rehabilitation tasks reveal how practice changes coordination over time.
focus: Measuring recovery during everyday movement rather than only during hospital visits.

name: Living Materials Collective
summary: Explores how bacteria and fungi can grow useful biodegradable materials. The team studies microbial communities that turn agricultural waste into lightweight packaging and self-repairing surfaces.
focus: Replacing difficult-to-recycle plastics with materials grown from renewable feedstocks.

name: Community Mobility Exchange
summary: Studies how bus schedules, housing costs, and job locations shape people's daily travel. Researchers combine transit-network models with resident diaries to identify transportation barriers.
focus: Making everyday trips to work, school, and healthcare easier without requiring a car.

name: Collective Learning Observatory
summary: Investigates how people teach one another in online communities. Experiments compare peer feedback, visual explanations, and collaborative problem solving across languages and age groups.
focus: Understanding which kinds of feedback help a learner transfer a skill to a new problem.

name: Battery Circularity Foundry
summary: Develops methods for recovering valuable metals from used rechargeable batteries. Electrochemical experiments connect material degradation to repair, reuse, and low-energy recycling processes.
focus: Keeping battery materials useful through multiple cycles of manufacturing and recovery.

name: Resilient Grids Lab
summary: Studies how neighborhoods can share solar electricity and stay powered during outages. Simulations coordinate batteries and flexible demand while measuring the effects on cost and reliability.
focus: Helping local energy networks recover when storms interrupt the larger electrical grid.

name: Sound and Memory Archive
summary: Explores how sounds preserve memories of changing places. Oral histories, acoustic recordings, and interactive maps let communities describe cultural experiences that are missing from written archives.
focus: Designing digital archives that preserve context and community ownership.

name: Tangible Information Studio
summary: Turns complex data into objects and interactive exhibits people can explore by touch. Designers study how physical interfaces communicate uncertainty and make information accessible beyond visual charts.
focus: Making scientific explanations useful to people with different sensory abilities.
